newsitem.title: USA: War of words continues on deal for Chicago airport.
newsitem.headline: War of words continues on deal for Chicago airport.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar and Chicago Mayor Richard Daley continued their verbal combat Thursday over a possible compromise that reportedly includes a small Chicago airport, a state bonding bill and a multi-purposed domed stadium.
An angry governor held a press availability in Springfield to lash out at the Daley Administration for comments made by unnamed city hall aides in a published report Wednesday.

The report in the Chicago Sun-Times suggested that Edgar had double-crossed Daley in the negotiations by signing into law Monday a bill allowing the state to take over Meigs Field on Chicago's downtown lakefront.
Edgar denied there was any agreement on the bill signing and warned that the report would not "bode well" in future discussions with the city.
"We'll continue to talk, but based on what happened, it will make it more difficult," Edgar said.
Daley, meanwhile, confirmed a meeting was held last Friday on Soldier Field, the current home of the Chicago Bears football team, which the mayor had proposed renovating.
He said his administration offered a compromise to state officials, however, he declined to say what was in the deal.
Edgar also refused to talk about the nature of the discussions.
According to the the Sun-Times report, the talks included an agreement for the state to drop its lawsuits to block city plans to turn the airport into a $27 million, bond-financed nature park.

In return, the newspaper said the governor would get a multi-pupose domed stadium in Chicago for use by the Bears and by conventions, as well as the mayor's help in getting Democratic lawmakers support for a $610 million general obligation bond authorization bill that the Republican governor wants.
Daley said his negotiators put a "good offer" on the table that would "satisfy all parties involved."
"I'm still at the table. If they want to walk away so be it," the mayor added.
